name: Runpod Serverless (per-worker inference endpoints)
price_basis: per WORKER-hour, not per GPU-hour - a worker is one GPU on Runpod's inference platform, so the two happen to coincide, but the unit is the thing you deploy. H200 $5.93; H100 $4.79; B200 $8.64; B300 $9.98; A100 $2.72; RTX 6000 Pro $3.49; L40/L40S/6000 Ada/MIG 48GB $1.75; A6000/A40 $1.22; 5090 $1.58; 24GB $1.10; 16GB $0.58. Page 'Updated September 27, 2026'; fetched 2026-10-03.
notes: IMPORTANT UNIT WARNING, because this is the one record in the slice where the natural unit is ambiguous: these are per-WORKER-hour rates for serverless inference endpoints, which is NOT the same thing as renting a GPU. You do not hold a GPU; you hold an endpoint that scales, and you are billed for the seconds a worker is processing. Runpod markets this as 'Save 25% over other Serverless cloud providers on flex workers alone' - a vendor claim. The practical comparison: serverless H100 at $4.79 is dearer per GPU-hour than the Runpod Pod rate ($3.49) and considerably dearer than the Pod rate on a provider like Vast.ai, but it includes autoscaling, cold-start management and an inference runtime, which is what you are actually buying. Compare it instead against CoreWeave's 'Inference Single GPU' H100 rate of $6.16 or Fireworks' dedicated H100 at $8.00 - on those three numbers Runpod serverless is the cheapest published serverless H100 in the slice, which is a real finding. If your load is steady, the Pod rate wins on raw price; if it is spiky, serverless wins on total cost, and Runpod says so itself.
